title: Choosing an inpaint route
hook: SetLatentNoiseMask, VAEEncodeForInpaint or InpaintModelConditioning: read what each one really does to your picture and your mask, then choose by model and denoise.

verified.claim: VAEEncodeForInpaint rounds the mask, grows it, greys the masked pixels, and stores the rounded grown mask. The lab's version gave the same mask and pixels as the real node with a pass-through VAE.
InpaintModelConditioning keeps the original in the latent, a soft noise_mask when enabled, and puts the greyed encode and the mask in the conditioning.

A checkpoint whose U-Net takes more than 4 channels gets concat_keys mask and masked_image; the SD 1.5 one has 9. concat_cond rounds the mask, and takes the masked image from concat_latent_image, or else from the latent.
Outside the mask the final latent equals the original, whichever route made it, with a sampler ending at sigma 0.

unchecked: No real model ran. The hole's numbers come from an exact denoiser for Gaussian content, which shows the arithmetic and cannot show picture quality.
Which route looks best on a given model is untested here. The recommendations follow from what each route feeds the model, not from a comparison of pictures.
With InpaintModelConditioning on models other than the SD inpainting family we read only the tooltip, which warns that noise_mask can improve or break results.
